objectives.statement: Explain the purpose of EXPLAIN as a way to inspect the query plan chosen by PostgreSQL.
Explain how an index can improve database performance by providing a faster access path to rows.
Identify ANALYZE as the command that collects table statistics used by the query planner.
Identify query-planning configuration as a way to influence the plans selected by the optimizer.
Interpret a basic EXPLAIN output as a tree of plan nodes with estimated cost and row information.
Identify B-tree as the default index type and recognize its common ordering and equality use cases.
Explain how planner statistics describe table contents and influence plan choices.
Distinguish routine VACUUM maintenance from the statistics collection performed by ANALYZE.
Explain that EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the statement while reporting actual execution information.
Explain how multicolumn indexes are organized and why column order matters for their use.
Explain how ANALYZE updates planner statistics in the pg_statistic catalog.
Identify planner cost constants as configuration values that affect estimated plan costs.
Distinguish sequential, index, and bitmap index scans as table access plan nodes.
Explain a partial index as an index built only over rows satisfying a predicate.
Explain how default_statistics_target controls the amount of statistics collected for columns.
Distinguish VACUUM from VACUUM FULL by their treatment of dead space and table rewriting.
Identify pg_stat_activity as the view that reports activity such as process state and current query.
Identify the role of parallel query plans in using multiple worker processes for eligible operations.
Explain how indexes can support ORDER BY operations when the requested ordering matches the index ordering.
Explain the role of the autovacuum daemon in automatically issuing maintenance and statistics operations when thresholds are reached.
